title: introduce-fragment-harmonizer-for-sse-reorder-and-delimiter-escape-guard
author: Priya Malhotra
ci_details: flaky-test-check: warn (1 flaky test fixed in follow-up)
release_notes: Fixes rare SSE interleaving that caused partial JSON fragments and mis-ordered function-call/tool sentinel emissions. Adds optional fragment harmonizer and delimiter-escape guard to improve streaming stability and OpenAI-compat edge cases.
description:
Problem and motivation:

Intermittent customer reports and internal canaries showed a class of SSE regressions where multi-event streams, combined with heartbeat events and backpressure, could produce: (a) partial JSON payloads emitted across separate SSE events that clients reassembled out-of-order, (b) function-call/tool sentinel tokens arriving before their trailing JSON payload, and (c) delimiter escape sequences being split such that JSON boundaries were ambiguous. Root cause analysis pointed to a small window in the async flush path where fragments from concurrent streams could be enqueued without a strict event-sequence anchor, and the existing streaming reassembly only did naive prefix concatenation.

What this PR does:

- Introduces a "fragment harmonizer" in the SSE server reassembly pipeline. Each outgoing stream now tags fragments with a lightweight monotonic fragment_id and per-event seq_no; the harmonizer uses a bounded reorder buffer (configurable 100ms/256 fragments) to re-sequence and coalesce fragments before the framing->wire encoder.
- Adds a delimiter-escape guard that scans potential boundary bytes when reassembling fragments and preserves an escape context across flush boundaries so we don't incorrectly treat an escaped newline/delimiter as an event boundary.
- Emits a backwards-compatible optional inline hint header (X-RI-Fragment-Hint) and a short inline marker (":frag\nid=<hex>\n") only when the harmonizer detects out-of-order fragments; this path is gated and off by default for public hosted flows but enabled for dedicated/private customers and in our e2e tests.
- Tightens the function-call sentinel handoff: tool/function tokens carry the originating event seq_no and are held until their trailing JSON is present or the reorder window completes; we fall back to the older streaming behavior after the window to avoid unbounded latency.
- Adds a suite of unit tests and deterministic e2e fixtures that reproduce the original failure modes (including artificially injected heartbeat jitter and partial flushes), and updates one doc page in the OpenAI-compat section describing the heuristics and opt-in header.

Design notes / tradeoffs:

- The harmonizer trades a bounded, configurable latency tail for correctness in pathological interleaving cases. In practice, our canaries show median latency impact <0.5ms and p99 within SLOs for affected flows.
- The inline frag hint is optional and only emitted in recovery scenarios to maintain compatibility with clients that don't understand it. No wire-level breaking change is introduced when the feature is off.
- We kept the reassembly logic intentionally conservative: the heuristic prefers correctness and predictable fallback behavior over aggressive speculative coalescing.

Review conversation (condensed chronological thread):

- James Liu (reviewer): "This looks promising. Please add metrics around reorder buffer occupancy and dropped-fragment events so we can detect when the window is insufficient in production. Also add a feature flag/FF gate for dedicated customers."

- Priya (author): "Added metrics: sse.reorder.window_ms, sse.reorder.max_held, sse.reorder.drop_count; feature gate toggle via ENV ENABLE_SSE_HARMONIZER and header flag X-RI-Fragment-Hint. Pushed new commit."

- Evan Brooks (reviewer): "Can you clarify the latency impact on streaming p99? The perf bench in CI shows a tiny regression on a high-qps microbenchmark."

- Priya: "Bench microbenchmark was synthetic; I added a production-like benchmark that keeps KV cache warm — p50/p95 unchanged, p99 increases by 0.8ms on a worst-case path. Added mitigation note and an autoscaling suggestion in the doc."

- Marisol Ortega (final approver): "LGTM after fixups. Please squash merge and add release note blurb."

CI timeline:

- Initial CI run: build+unit-tests+lint passed, e2e failed due to flaky test in unrelated tracing harness (test fixture ordering).
- Re-run after small test harness fix: all checks green. Perf-bench run completed; flagged as acceptable by SRE.

Merge outcome:

- Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-21 by Marisol Ortega. Commit message points to ENG-9210.

Follow-ups / operational notes:

- Enable ENABLE_SSE_HARMONIZER in selected Dedicated clusters for a 2-week ramp to surface any remaining edge cases; dashboard added to Redwood Console under "SSE Fragment Harmonizer" showing reorder metrics.
- Plan a small follow-up to add a server-side opt-out header for latency-critical customers and to backfill one flaky test flagged during CI.
